findings.detail: scored 0 — The answer declares the standard 4/7/10 buffers adequate at pH 3 (the prohibited claim) and misses four of the five must-contain points including the need for a pH 1.68/2 buffer the bracketing requirement the 10 C buffer-temperature rule and the 0.05 pH-unit check. Unmet: States the usual 4/7/10 buffer set is not sufficient for acidic water and a pH 1.68 (or 2) buffer is needed when acidic waters are measured; States the sample pH must fall inside the calibrated range so a 4/7/10 set does not bracket pH 3.2; States the calibration buffers must be within about 10 C of the sample temperature; States that a check of the buffer nearest the sample pH should be within about 0.05 pH unit of its value at that temperature or the system is recalibrated

scored 0 — The answer correctly states the subsample qualifier rule for turbidity temperature DO and Eh but it refuses the flow-cell sampling question and omits the storage limits and time-sensitivity guidance withholding facts the rubric expects. Unmet: States plainly that a discrete turbidity sample must not be collected from the discharge passing through the flow-through chamber holding the other sensors; Gives the storage limits if the sample cannot be read on site: clean amber bottle kept out of sunlight chilled at or below 4 C held no longer than 24 hours; Notes turbidity is time sensitive and should be measured on site preferably in situ

scored 0 — The answer misses all four must-contain points: it declines to compare the two tables rather than stating they agree never notes that A6.0 points multiparameter users to A6.8 omits the standard-criteria/accuracy-varies point and gives no persistent-variability procedure. Unmet: States plainly that the two tables give the same stabilisation criteria and do not conflict; States the general field-measurement chapter points multiparameter users to the multiparameter chapter for criteria of the same kind; States the criteria are standard sensor stabilisation criteria and that actual sensor accuracy varies by model and manufacturer; For persistent variability extends equilibration and records additional measurements then reports the median of the final five or more readings or selects a representative final reading with documented judgment

scored 0 — The answer is a refusal that supplies none of the required table values the 0.03 mg/L difference the Benson and Krause basis the tolerance comparison or the advice to use one protocol's table consistently so every must-contain point is missed. Unmet: Gives the USGS table value at 20.0 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.09 mg/L; Gives the EPA chart value at 20 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.06 mg/L; States the difference is 0.03 mg/L and assesses its significance against the applicable procedure; Notes the USGS values are generated from the Benson and Krause equations; Compares the 0.03 mg/L difference with the USGS saturation-check tolerance of ±0.2 mg/L; Advises using the table belonging to whichever protocol the work is being done under consistently

scored 0 — The answer gives the multiplication method and cites table 6.2-4 but withholds the required factor 0.8235 saying it lacks the information which is a refusal of a figure the rubric asks for. Unmet: Gives 0.8235 as the factor for 20.0 °C at 50 000 µS/cm

scored 0 — The answer approves diluting a strong commercial stock down generally presenting the 4 000-unit formazin dilution as the general procedure which violates the must-not items against approving dilution of commercial standards and treating the formazin exception as universal. Unmet: states that commercial calibration solutions must not be diluted; gives 4 000-unit formazin as the one exception that may be diluted; explains that diluting changes the suspension matrix so the dilutions are no longer linear; recommends buying commercially prepared solutions at the values needed rather than preparing them by dilution

scored 0 — The answer describes a ZoBell's check but omits the timing (before field measurements) and all three specific acceptance figures — the 5 mV agreement with the table value the 430 mV theoretical Eh at 25 °C and the ±5 mV stabilization — so no must-contain point is made; it commits no must-not violation. Unmet: States the check is made against ZoBell's solution before field measurements; States the calculated Eh of ZoBell's must come within 5 mV of the table value for the solution's temperature; Gives 430 mV as the theoretical Eh of ZoBell's at 25 °C; States the reading must stabilize to within ±5 mV before the temperature and millivolt value are recorded

scored 0 — The answer places pH before specific conductance ("do pH conductivity and ORP first") violating a must-not item and misses the temperature-first conductivity-before-pH DO-then-ORP ordering and the ionic-strength carryover rationale. Unmet: Places temperature first in the sequence; Places specific conductance before pH; Places dissolved oxygen and then oxidation-reduction potential after pH; Explains that the sequence runs from lower to higher ionic strength so carryover from one standard does not bias the next; Notes specifically that pH buffers and electrode filling solutions are high in ionic strength and would contaminate a conductivity calibration

scored 0 — The answer is a bare refusal that makes none of the required must-contain points about the turbidity fouling check the EPA SOP's pre/post-calibration comparison or the absence of a keep-or-discard rule and cites no sources. Unmet: States the corpus gives no rule for deciding which part of a long record may be kept and which must be thrown out; States no source gives an allowable rate of drift (per-day or per-week) for a sensor left in the water; States it gives no procedure for correcting or adjusting a record after the instrument comes out; Notes the turbidity chapter offers a fouling check comparing the sensor's reading on a calibrant before and after cleaning taking the percent difference; States the fouling check quantifies one sensor's condition and is not an acceptance rule for the record; Notes the EPA field calibration SOP has the operator calibrate before deployment and check on recovery defers drift criteria to the project QA plan and supplies default post-calibration criteria only when that plan is silent; Declines to convert the EPA post-calibration criteria into a keep-or-discard threshold for a month of record and supplies no drift tolerance beyond them; Notes the EPA SOP's default post-calibration criteria are a pass-or-fail check on the instrument at recovery not a rule for how much of the record may be kept and that data failing the check are qualified rather than discarded
